articles.title: The Science Behind Haldi Doodh: Why Turmeric Milk May Improve Your Sleep
articles.excerpt: The ancient Indian drink combines anti-inflammatory curcumin with calming spices, and modern research is beginning to validate what generations of Indian families already knew.
articles.nri_angle: Haldi doodh is a cherished Indian tradition that diaspora families continue to practise, now supported by growing scientific evidence for its health benefits.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rahul Roy Opens Up About Speech Recovery Six Years After Brain Stroke
articles.excerpt: The Aashiqui actor says he takes eight medicines daily and has switched to a vegan diet since suffering a cerebrovascular stroke in 2020.
articles.nri_angle: Rahul Roy's recovery story resonates with Indian diaspora families familiar with the Aashiqui-era actor and the realities of stroke rehabilitation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Viral Kora Turmeric Mask: What This Desi Skincare Hack Can and Cannot Do
articles.excerpt: A DIY face mask using raw turmeric, rice flour, gram flour, and yogurt has taken social media by storm. Dermatologists say the ingredients have real benefits — but with important caveats.
articles.image_caption: A woman applies a turmeric-based face pack at home. The viral kora turmeric mask combines dry-roasted raw turmeric with gram flour, rice flour, and yogurt for a traditional Indian skincare treatment.
articles.nri_angle: The kora turmeric mask draws directly from Indian beauty traditions that diaspora families have practiced for generations, now finding a global audience through social media.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Curcumin in Turmeric May Protect Blood Vessels From Diabetes Damage, Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A study in rats presented at the American Physiology Summit shows that curcumin reduced inflammation and restored vascular function in Type 1 diabetes, though human trials are still needed.
articles.image_caption: A turmeric plant in bloom. A new study finds curcumin, the active compound in turmeric, may help protect blood vessels from diabetes-related damage.
articles.nri_angle: Turmeric is a cornerstone of Indian cuisine and traditional medicine, and this research adds scientific backing to its long-held health reputation among the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Just Four Weeks on a Vegan Diet Can Shift Genes Linked to Inflammation and Aging, Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A UC San Diego study found measurable epigenetic changes in healthy adults after one month on a plant-based diet — findings that echo the vegetarian traditions long practiced across the Indian subcontinent
articles.nri_angle: The findings resonate with Indian dietary traditions, where vegetarian and plant-forward diets have been practiced for centuries across Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism. India has the world's largest vegetarian population, and the study adds scientific backing to these long-held cultural practices.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Sugary Drink a Day More Than Doubles Stomach Cancer Risk, Landmark U.S. Study Finds
articles.excerpt: Mass General Brigham researchers analyzed data from 112,000 adults over decades and found a 2.45 times higher risk of gastric cancer among daily consumers of sugar-sweetened beverages
articles.nri_angle: The findings are relevant for the Indian diaspora, where sugary drinks and sweetened beverages are widely consumed and stomach cancer rates among South Asians remain a concern.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Even Light Exercise Lowers Stroke and Death Risk for People With AFib, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A 15-year study of 87,000 adults found that even low levels of physical activity reduced stroke risk by 9% and extended life by up to 1.2 years for those with atrial fibrillation
articles.nri_angle: Atrial fibrillation affects an estimated 10.55 million Americans, including South Asian Americans who face elevated cardiovascular risk due to genetic and lifestyle factors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CAR T-Cell Therapy Puts Severe Rheumatoid Arthritis Into Remission in Landmark First Trial
articles.excerpt: Three of six patients achieved sustained medication-free remission after a single infusion in the world's first CAR T-cell trial for rheumatoid arthritis
articles.nri_angle: Rheumatoid arthritis prevalence in South Asia and significance of breakthrough treatments for the Indian diaspora community
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shingles Vaccine Linked to Lower Heart Attack and Stroke Risk, Major Studies Find
articles.excerpt: A study published in Nature found the newer shingles vaccine reduced cardiovascular burden by 9% over seven years, adding to earlier research showing vaccinated heart patients were 46% less likely to suffer a serious cardiac event.
articles.image_caption: Shingles vaccine vials. Multiple large-scale studies have linked the recombinant shingles vaccine to significantly reduced risk of heart attack and stroke.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face disproportionately higher cardiovascular disease rates, making the shingles vaccine's newly discovered heart benefits especially relevant for Indian American adults over 50.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi H1N1 Cases Cross 2,600 as Hospitals Scale Up Isolation Wards
articles.excerpt: India's capital has recorded around 3,000 influenza cases this year, with H1N1 accounting for nearly three-quarters of all Influenza A infections. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has called an emergency review meeting.
articles.nri_angle: Health advisory for NRIs and Indian Americans planning travel to Delhi during the monsoon season amid a sixfold surge in H1N1 influenza cases.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Women With Type 2 Diabetes Face Higher Mental Health Risk Than Men, UK Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A study of nearly 29,000 UK patients reveals that women are 53% more likely to develop mental health conditions after a type 2 diabetes diagnosis, while men face higher cardiovascular and kidney risks.
articles.nri_angle: Type 2 diabetes is disproportionately prevalent in South Asian populations, making sex-specific care insights especially relevant for the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Scientists Develop RK-251, a Smart Cancer Drug That Activates Only Inside Tumour Cells
articles.excerpt: Researchers at IASST and IIT Guwahati have created a drug candidate that uses cancer cells' own chemistry to trigger its anticancer payload, potentially reducing chemotherapy's collateral damage.
articles.image_caption: A researcher works in a laboratory setting. Indian scientists at IASST and IIT Guwahati have developed RK-251, a drug candidate designed to activate only inside cancer cells.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin researchers and diaspora families following cancer treatment advances will note this contribution from Indian institutions to global oncology research, with potential implications for treatment access in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Landmark Trial Shows 4 in 5 Rectal Cancer Patients Can Avoid Major Surgery
articles.excerpt: The STAR-TREC trial, published in The Lancet Oncology, found that chemoradiotherapy allowed most early-stage rectal cancer patients to keep their rectum and skip radical surgery.
articles.image_caption: A radiotherapy machine in a hospital clinical setting. The STAR-TREC trial found that chemoradiotherapy can allow most early-stage rectal cancer patients to avoid radical surgery.
articles.nri_angle: Colorectal cancer incidence is rising among Indian and South Asian populations globally, making advances in less invasive treatment options directly relevant to diaspora families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Doctors Urge Early Action on Malaria and Dengue as India's Monsoon Season Peaks
articles.excerpt: Health experts warn that dismissing early symptoms as routine viral fever is the most common and dangerous mistake during monsoon months, when all Indian states except Ladakh are endemic to mosquito-borne diseases.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs planning monsoon-season visits to India should be aware of malaria and dengue warning signs and consult travel health specialists before departure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Woman Develops Severe Brain Disorder After 15-Day Water-Only Diet, May Never Walk Normally Again
articles.excerpt: Doctors diagnose Wernicke's encephalopathy after a Chinese woman's extreme fast depleted her vitamin B1 reserves, leaving her with a 'penguin-like' gait that may be permanent.
articles.image_caption: Wernicke's encephalopathy, a severe brain disorder caused by vitamin B1 deficiency. A 31-year-old woman developed the condition after a 15-day water-only fast.
articles.nri_angle: Extreme fasting trends, including practices rooted in traditional Eastern medicine, have gained popularity globally; the case serves as a health warning for communities where prolonged fasting is culturally practiced.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: PM2.5 Pollution Linked to Millions of Cancer Cases Beyond the Lungs, Nature Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A sweeping analysis across 952 global locations ties long-term fine particle exposure to cancers of the breast, digestive tract, and liver — with South Asia bearing a disproportionate burden.
articles.image_caption: Airborne particulate pollution. A major study in Nature links PM2.5 exposure to millions of cancer cases beyond the lungs, affecting multiple organ systems.
articles.nri_angle: Indian cities face some of the world’s worst PM2.5 levels, making this study directly relevant to families in India and diaspora members concerned about relatives’ health.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Australian Baby First in World to Receive Precision Treatment for Rare Epilepsy
articles.excerpt: Eight-month-old Bodhi went from 50 seizures a day to virtually none within weeks, while Indian doctors advance VNS therapy for drug-resistant cases.
articles.image_caption: An Australian infant has become the first in the world to receive a precision gene therapy treatment for a rare form of epilepsy.
articles.nri_angle: Indian doctors at CARE Hospitals Hyderabad are advancing VNS therapy for drug-resistant epilepsy, highlighting India’s growing capacity in neurological care.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Twenty Minutes of Exercise Works as Well as a Nap to Rescue a Sleep-Deprived Brain
articles.excerpt: A McGill University study finds both a short workout and a 90-minute nap boost memory by 22% after 30 hours without sleep — but through different brain pathways.
articles.image_caption: New research finds that just 20 minutes of exercise can restore cognitive function as effectively as a nap for sleep-deprived individuals.
articles.nri_angle: Sleep deprivation is a widespread concern for diaspora professionals and shift workers; the study offers a practical intervention accessible to anyone with 20 minutes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
